slides.title: Tensors & Keras
slides.content:
# The Tensor 📦

A multi-dimensional array that flows through the graph.

## Keras API
TensorFlow includes **Keras**, a high-level API to build models easily.

```tf
import tensorflow as tf

# Creating a sequential model
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(128, activation='relu'),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])
```

slides.title: Training
slides.content:
# Compile & Fit 🏃

1. **Compile**: Define optimizer, loss function, and metrics.
2. **Fit**: Train the model on data.

```tf
model.compile(
    optimizer='adam',
    loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
    metrics=['accuracy']
)

# Train for 5 epochs
model.fit(x_train, y_train, epochs=5)
```

slides.title: Eager Execution
slides.content:
# Immediate Results ⚡

Older TensorFlow required building a static graph first. Modern TensorFlow (2.0+) uses **Eager Execution** by default.

Operations are evaluated immediately as they are called from Python.
```tf
x = [[2.]]
m = tf.matmul(x, x)
print(m) # tf.Tensor([[4.]], shape=(1, 1), dtype=float32)
```
